title: UDim2
summary: 2D GUI size/position value combining SCALE (fraction of parent, resolution-independent) and OFFSET (pixels). UDim2.fromScale, fromOffset, or new(scaleX, offX, scaleY, offY).

reference.signature: UDim2.new(xScale, xOffset, yScale, yOffset) / UDim2.fromScale(x, y) / UDim2.fromOffset(x, y)

explanation.whatItIs: GUI measurement with two dials per axis: a percentage of the parent, plus fixed pixels. Mix them freely.
explanation.whyItExists: Screens come in every size; pure pixels break, pure percentages can't express 'exactly 300px'. Scale+Offset does both.
whenToUse: Mixes: full width minus margins — UDim2.new(1, -20, 0, 40)
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
UDim2.new(scaleX, offX, scaleY, offY)
          │        │
          │        └─ pixels (fixed)
          └─ fraction of parent (responsive)

(1, -20, 0, 40) = full width minus 20px, 40px tall
```
tips: Design in Scale for structure, Offset for fine detail
AbsoluteSize tells you the resolved pixels after layout
commonMistakes: Confusing argument order: X(scale,offset) then Y(scale,offset)
Negative scale confusion: scale fractions can be negative too

examples.title: Responsive centered panel
examples.code:
local panel = Instance.new("Frame")
panel.Size = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.4, 0)      -- 50% wide, 40% tall
panel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
panel.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)  -- dead center

local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
bar.Size = UDim2.new(1, -16, 0, 12)         -- full width minus 16px, 12px tall
bar.Parent = panel
